card.name: Chapter abbreviations and 'good news' wording
card.fires_on: The word 'chap' (chapter) in book citations, and the word just before 'news' in 'good news' or 'joyous news' in gospel passages. It also fires on scattered words in older prose.

modes.label: Chapter citations
modes.description: The abbreviation 'Chap' or 'chap' in a book or reference citation before a chapter number.
modes.example: Comprehensive Gynecology. 5th ed. Philadelphia, Pa: Mosby Elsevier; 2007:<< chap>> 41.

modes.label: Good news in gospel text
modes.description: The word 'good' or 'joyous' just before 'news' when describing the gospel.
modes.example: Gentiles were saved by believing the<< good>> news that

modes.label: Old-style prose
modes.description: Scattered words in historical or archaic writing, often partway through a phrase.
modes.example: would deserve<< better>> of mankind, and do more essential service
